review_reason: Footnote [a] of Table 1, the table holding the frozen anchor, states: "The absolute configuration of product was determined to be S by comparison of the specific rotations with the literature data." The anchor is the QuinoxP* model-substrate entry of that same table. Not inferred from the ee.

The main-article table footnote states: "1a (0.2 mmol), solvent (1 mL), the absolute configuration of product was determined as R by comparison of the specific rotations with the literature data." The frozen anchor is the SI general procedure 1a to 2a, the same transformation, but the statement sits in the main article rather than in the anchor itself. Reviewer should confirm the cross-reference.

The main text reports the product as (R)-GVL ("levulinic acid from biomass feedstock transformed into (R)-GVL", Scheme 8B) and the computational section states the hydrogenation "should give the R configuration product", consistent with the experimental 95% ee. The assignment is product-level rather than printed in Table 1 entry 1; reviewer should confirm it applies to the Ni(OTf)2/(S,S)-Ph-BPE entry.

review_reason: The SI characterizes the hydrogenation product of acetophenone as "(S)-1-Phenylethanol (4a)" with [a]20D = -55.3 (c 0.88, CHCl3). The frozen anchor is the large-scale run in eq 4, which gives the same product from the same substrate and catalyst; the configuration is a property of that product. Reviewer should confirm the cross-reference to the large-scale entry.

The text naming the frozen anchor states: "(S)-Ibuprofen ((S)-2l) could be obtained via asymmetric hydrogenation of 1l using a catalyst loading of 0.10 mol% (1000 S/C) (Fig. 3c, 99% yield and 96% ee)." This is the anchor's own sentence. Note the paper separately assigns product 2f as R by X-ray; that is a different substrate and is not used here.

The footnote immediately preceding Table 2 states: "The absolute configuration was assigned by comparing the sign of the optical rotation of the product 2a, methyl (R)-3-acetamido-3-phenylpropanoate, with that reported in the literature." The frozen anchor is Table 2 entry 2, whose product is 2a.

The SI titles the product "(R)-1-(sec-butyl)-4-methoxybenzene (2a)", but the measured rotation is [a]20D = -23.2 (c 1.11, CHCl3) against a cited literature value of [a]23D = +27.0 (c 1.0, CHCl3) for 94% ee. The opposite sign is not explained in the text, so the printed descriptor and the measured rotation disagree on their face. A chemist must resolve which enantiomer this is before the slot is filled; the proposal records only what the SI literally prints.

No absolute configuration is stated anywhere in the article or its SI: a search for "absolute configuration", an assignment phrase, an optical rotation and any (R)/(S) product descriptor returns nothing. Table 2 carries only conv. (%) and e.e. (%) columns, confirmed by visual inspection of the typeset table, and its single footnote only defines S, C and B. The slot was looked for and the source does not report it.
